artists.biography:
Therapy? are a rock band from Northern Ireland. The band was formed in 1989 by guitarist-vocalist Andy Cairns from Ballyclare and drummer-vocalist Fyfe Ewing. Therapy? recorded their first demo with Cairns filling in on bass guitar. To complete the lineup, the band recruited Larne bassist Michael McKeegan. The band signed with major label A&M Records in 1992, for which they released four albums, most notably Troublegum in 1994 and Infernal Love in 1995. Ewing's departure in early 1996 preceded the arrivals of his replacement Graham Hopkins, and Martin McCarrick on cello and guitar. Neil Cooper replaced Hopkins on drums in 2002. Following the departure of McCarrick in 2004, the band have remained a stable three-piece since.

Therapy? are currently signed to UK independent label Marshall Records. The band has released 15 full-length studio albums and has sold over two million albums worldwide.

perplexity.description:
Infernal Love," released in 1995 by Therapy? on A&M Records and later reissued by Music On Vinyl, is a darker, more introspective follow-up to their breakthrough album "Troublegum" (1994). While "Troublegum" combined melodic punk and metal to broad commercial success, "Infernal Love" explores a moodier, more atmospheric rock sound with elements of grit and rawness, drawing comparisons to bands like Afghan Whigs and Hüsker Dü. The album was produced by Al Clay at Real World Studios, where the band embraced a more experimental approach, leaving space for textured guitar sounds and emotional depth in the songwriting.

Positioned as a significant evolution in Therapy?'s discography, "Infernal Love" reflects a period of intense creative pressure following their global breakthrough. It balances the band's aggressive roots with a more nuanced, sometimes brooding tone, marking a deliberate shift from the high-energy punk-metal fusion of its predecessor. Critically, the album was well received for its artistic ambition and complexity, maintaining the band's momentum in the mid-1990s alternative rock scene, though it did not replicate the same level of commercial success as "Troublegum".
